title: Day 2 Activity and Assignment
summary: Discuss workplace scenarios involving disrespect, exclusion and gossip, then demonstrate three deliberate acts of respect during your shift.

sections.title: Activity: Discuss workplace scenarios
paragraphs: In small groups, discuss the three scenarios below.
Use what you learned in Day 2 about respect, boundaries, gossip, cliques, courtesy, personal feelings and confidentiality.
Focus on the behaviour, the effect on the team and the professional response — not on naming real colleagues.

sections.title: Scenario 1 — Disrespect
paragraphs: A new therapist makes a mistake while arranging massage supplies. An experienced therapist laughs and says: "Even this simple thing, you don't know how to do it?" Other staff begin laughing.
The new therapist becomes reluctant to ask questions.
list: Which Day 2 principle has been broken?
How might this affect the new therapist and client service?
What should the experienced therapist have said instead?
What should other staff do if they witness this?

sections.title: Scenario 2 — Exclusion
paragraphs: Three therapists are close friends. Whenever a new therapist joins, they avoid including her in conversations about work procedures and refuse to assist her when she needs guidance.
The new therapist struggles to understand the workplace.
list: When does a friendship group become an unhealthy clique?
Does friendship give anyone the right to withhold work information?
How could exclusion affect service quality?
What should the existing therapists do differently?

sections.title: Scenario 3 — Gossip
paragraphs: A staff member hears that another employee may be leaving Zura Spa. Instead of checking whether the information is appropriate to discuss, she tells several colleagues that the employee has been dismissed.
The information is incorrect. The rumour spreads.
list: What was wrong with the employee's behaviour?
How is this different from reporting a genuine concern to a supervisor?
What should you say if a colleague starts this conversation with you?
What should the employee do after discovering the information was false?

sections.title: Discussion prompts for every scenario
list: What is the actual issue — not the personality?
Who is affected besides the people in the room?
What would a courteous, professional response sound like?
When should a supervisor be involved?
How does confidentiality apply?

sections.title: Assignment: Three deliberate acts of respect
paragraphs: During your next shift, demonstrate three deliberate acts of respect toward colleagues.
Deliberate means you choose the action on purpose — it is not accidental politeness.
Write down what you did, who it supported (without gossiping about private details), and how it helped the team.

sections.title: Examples of deliberate respect
list: Greet a colleague you do not usually speak to and include her in a work-related update.
Ask permission before using a colleague's belongings.
Correct a mistake privately and show the proper procedure.
Refuse to join a rumour and redirect the concern to the right person.
Share necessary appointment or room information even if you are still upset with the colleague.
Thank a colleague for covering a duty or for a job well done.
Speak respectfully about a colleague who is not in the room.
Welcome a new or less-experienced staff member and offer appropriate guidance.

sections.title: How to complete the assignment
list: Act 1: Describe the situation, what you did, and why it showed respect.
Act 2: Describe the situation, what you did, and why it showed respect.
Act 3: Describe the situation, what you did, and why it showed respect.
Note one thing you will continue doing after this shift.

remember: Respect is shown in ordinary moments: how you speak, who you include, and whether you refuse gossip. Complete the discussion, then practise three deliberate acts of respect on the floor.
